entries.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury (Stablecoin Certification Review Committee)
entries.title: Treasury files an interim final rule setting the forms and procedures for reviewing State payment-stablecoin certifications under GENIUS Act section 4(c)
entries.facts: On September 29, 2026 the Department of the Treasury filed for Federal Register public inspection an interim final rule issued on behalf of the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee (document 2026-19966, RIN 1505-AC97, docket TREAS-DO-2026-0562), scheduled for publication on September 30, 2026. The document states: "The Department of the Treasury is issuing this interim final rule on behalf of the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee (Committee). The Committee is adopting interim procedural regulations and forms to implement its responsibilities under section 4(c) of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act or the Act). The regulations set out a process to facilitate the Committee's approval or denial of certifications submitted by State payment stablecoin regulators under section 4(c)(4) of the GENIUS Act, and prescribe the form of such certifications." The filed text sets out an initial certification package consisting of a signed attestation that the State regime meets the substantial-similarity criteria, a narrative demonstrating compliance, and supporting statutes, regulations and guidance; an annual recertification package; a 30-day Committee review period; a 180-day cure period following a denial, or two years where the trigger is a change in Federal law; quarterly recertification submission windows keyed to the approval anniversary; suspension of a certification where an annual recertification is not timely filed; electronic submission to a Treasury email address; and appeal of a final denial to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit. On timing, the filed document states: "Effective date: This interim final rule is effective [INSERT DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]; however, certifications will not be accepted until after Paperwork Reduction Act approval of the information collection. Treasury will post a notification on its website as to when certifications will be accepted." It also states: "Comments on this interim final rule must be received on or before [INSERT DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]." Both bracketed dates are unfilled in the filed text. The Federal Register record lists the document as 55 pages.
entries.source_label: Federal Register public inspection — Treasury interim final rule, document 2026-19966 (filed September 29, 2026)
entries.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers, State payment stablecoin regulators, banks and payment processors, crypto exchanges

entries.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control
entries.title: OFAC final rule removes the authorization for U.S. banking institutions to process Cuba-related "U-turn" funds transfers and replaces it with an authorization to reject them
entries.facts: On September 29, 2026 the Office of Foreign Assets Control filed for Federal Register public inspection a final rule amending the Cuban Assets Control Regulations, 31 CFR part 515 (document 2026-19973), scheduled for publication on September 30, 2026. The document's summary states: "The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is amending the Cuban Assets Control Regulations to implement portions of the President's foreign policy toward Cuba, including as directed by National Security Presidential Memorandum-5". On funds transfers, the rule states: "OFAC is amending Sec. 515.584(d) to remove the authorization for banking institutions subject to U.S. jurisdiction to process these 'U-Turn' transactions and to replace it with an authorization to reject such transactions." The amended section is reproduced in the filed text as authorizing a banking institution subject to U.S. jurisdiction to reject funds transfers originating and terminating outside the United States where the stated conditions apply. The rule also revises 31 CFR 515.209 so that indirect as well as direct financial transactions with entities and subentities on the Cuba Restricted List are prohibited, and states: "A person engages in an indirect financial transaction by participating in a transfer of funds, but not acting as an originator or ultimate beneficiary, where either the originator or the ultimate beneficiary is an entity or subentity on the Cuba Restricted List." The sections listed as amended, added, revised or removed are 31 CFR 515.201, 515.209, 515.421, 515.530, 515.534, 515.542, 515.545, 515.547, 515.560, 515.561, 515.564, 515.565, 515.566, 515.567, 515.570, 515.572, 515.573, 515.574, 515.576, 515.577, 515.578, 515.581, 515.584, 515.590 and 515.591. On timing the filed document states: "This rule is effective [INSERT DATE OF PUBLICATION IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]" — an unfilled bracket in the filed text.

entries.title: SEC charges four entities over WhatsApp group-chat schemes that allegedly induced investors to transfer crypto assets to fake trading platforms
entries.facts: On September 29, 2026 the Securities and Exchange Commission issued press release 2026-95, "SEC Charges Multiple Entities in Fraud Schemes Totaling at Least $15 Million that Used WhatsApp and Other Platforms to Lure Investors," and companion Litigation Release 26654. The releases name four defendants: Cryptoaiml Ltd., Cryptoaiml Capital Foundation, TSAI Pro Ltd. and TSAI Capital Foundation. The Commission states that "the entities formed WhatsApp group chats where they gained investor trust by impersonating investment professionals and issuing supposed AI-generated trading 'signals' or tips claiming to produce large profits. The defendants allegedly directed investors and clients to open accounts on their fake trading platform and manipulated them into transferring crypto assets to the platform." The releases further state that investors who attempted to withdraw funds were told their accounts were frozen until they paid fraudulent advance fees, and that the TSAI entities represented that investors could earn money "by depositing funds on their online platform for the purpose of renting bots programmed with artificial intelligence to trade on investors' behalf," and falsely claimed to be SEC-regulated while posting fraudulent certificates. The Commission attributes approximately $12.5 million in misappropriated funds to the Cryptoaiml entities and approximately $2.8 million to the TSAI entities. The cases are captioned SEC v. Cryptoaiml Ltd.; Cryptoaiml Capital Foundation, No. 26-civ-08508 (S.D.N.Y.) and SEC v. TSAI Pro Ltd.; TSAI Capital Foundation, No. 26-civ-08518 (S.D.N.Y.). The Commission dates the Cryptoaiml conduct to August 2024 through March 2025 and the TSAI conduct to September 2024 through March 2025, and states that it seeks permanent injunctions, conduct-based injunctions, disgorgement of ill-gotten gains with prejudgment interest, and civil penalties. The allegations have not been proven; the Commission's complaints set out charges that remain to be adjudicated.
entries.source_label: SEC press release 2026-95 (September 29, 2026), with companion Litigation Release 26654
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges and custodians, brokerages, payment processors, fraud and compliance teams
